keyVerseText: And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim. Dodanim: or, as some read it, Rodanim
rootMeaning: The name אֱלִישָׁה (ʼĔlîyshâh) is likely of foreign derivation, as indicated by the lexicon, and is understood to mean "God of the coming (one)." This suggests a compound of elements referring to God (El) and a notion of arrival or future presence (coming one). Unlike a simple proper name, this root sense carries a theological nuance pointing to God's active involvement in what is to come, highlighting divine sovereignty over future events.
usageInScripture: The term אֱלִישָׁה appears three times in Scripture, consistently rendered as 'Elishah' or 'of Elishah,' reflecting its use as a proper name. It identifies a son of Javan and a descendant of Noah, possibly linked to ancient peoples such as the Aeolians. This consistency in translation underscores its function as a genealogical marker rather than a common noun, anchoring historical identity within the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֱלִישָׁה as 'God of the coming (one)' enriches our grasp of God's providential role in history, especially in the unfolding of nations and peoples. It reminds believers that God is sovereign not only over individuals but also over entire lineages and the destiny of peoples. This name, tied to a descendant of Noah, connects the faith story to God's covenantal promises extending through generations, ultimately fulfilled in Christ. Thus, Elishah embodies the faithfulness of God to His unfolding plan, encouraging trust in His control over the future.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 10:4 lists Elishah among the sons of Javan, emphasizing his role as a progenitor of certain peoples. The name Elishah here contributes more than genealogical information; it signals God's providential hand in the establishment of nations. Recognizing Elishah as 'God of the coming (one)' invites reflection on how God ordains the rise of peoples and cultures according to His sovereign will, a theme that resonates throughout Scripture.
